page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose, seventh-generation instance type built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Powered by a custom Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, this instance features 1 physical CPU core, 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading, and 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Network performance is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs are included with this instance profile.

In performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates moderate single-core capabilities but exhibits limitations under multi-threaded workloads. Single-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench single-core scores place in the average benchmark tier, supported by single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core performance, rate in the poor to weak tiers due to the single physical core footprint. Memory bandwidth read and write metrics also fall into lower performance categories, impacting memory-intensive benchmarks like PassMark memory and database operations.

From a resource density perspective, the instance provides a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for entry-level modern workloads requiring updated x86_64 vector instructions. Key tradeoffs include restricted aggregate throughput and lower memory bandwidth density. Appropriate workloads for this instance type include lightweight web microservices, general purpose application servers, small background task processing, and development or testing environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is an entry-level general-purpose cloud server powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor with 1 physical core, 2 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction acceleration features like AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results highlight average single-core performance suitable for single-threaded tasks, alongside weak to poor multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth due to its single-core resource allocation. With a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps and no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, the instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It is best suited for small application backends, basic web serving, light utility tasks, and development environments requiring updated CPU feature sets.
